s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive headache and vomiting with a mass in the left frontal and temporal convexity
salient_findings: Large extra-axial heterogeneous mass over the left frontal and temporal convexity
key_facts: 19-year-old man
No significant medical history
2-week history of progressive headache
Two episodes of vomiting
12-month history of apathy and declining academic performance
Right pronator drift on neurologic examination
Normal remainder of neurologic examination
Large extra-axial heterogeneous mass over the left frontal and temporal convexity on CT
Erosion of the inner table of the left frontal bone
Near-complete erosion of the outer table of the left frontal bone
Heterogeneous enhancement and susceptibility artifacts on MRI
Evidence of calvarial destruction and a small extracranial component

shortlist.label: Hemangiopericytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Entertained as a diagnosis based on imaging findings and planned surgical resection

shortlist.label: Meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Common extra-axial tumor with heterogeneous enhancement and calcification, consistent with imaging findings

shortlist.label: Osteosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive bone tumor with potential for extracranial component and calvarial destruction

shortlist.label: Chordoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare tumor with potential for skull base involvement and heterogeneous enhancement

shortlist.label: Ewing's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive tumor with potential for extracranial component and calvarial destruction, although less common in this location

raw.rationale: The presence of a large extra-axial heterogeneous mass with well-defined lobulated margins, avid enhancement of denser areas, and evidence of calvarial destruction is consistent with hemangiopericytoma, which is a rare tumor that can cause bone erosion and has a variable appearance on imaging.

rejected.label: Meningioma
rejected.why: Meningiomas are typically more homogeneous and have a dural tail sign, which is not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Osteosarcoma
rejected.why: Osteosarcomas are primary bone tumors that would not typically present as an extra-axial mass.

rejected.label: Chordoma
rejected.why: Chordomas are midline tumors that often involve the clivus or sacrum, and are not typically found in the frontal convexity.

rejected.label: Ewing's sarcoma
rejected.why: Ewing's sarcoma is a primary bone tumor that would not typically present as an extra-axial mass with the described imaging characteristics.
